class_evidence: Main paper: seven image datasets, all multiclass with selected classes kept: MNIST and Fashion-MNIST (10 classes, IR 100; Sec. 4.1, Table 1), CIFAR10 and SVHN (10 classes; Sec. 4.2, Table 2), CelebA and LSUN (5 classes, small and large; Sec. 4.3, Table 3), SUN397 (50 classes; Sec. 4.4, Table 4). Supplement (Sec. 4, Tables 7-8, p.8): GAMO also run on three two-class sets (Abalone19, IJCNN1, Magic) and two multiclass sets with all classes kept (Chess 18 classes, Cover Type 7).
reduced_multiclass: None in the main paper. Supplement uses Abalone19, the KEEL two-class version of Abalone (reduction not described); IJCNN1 and Magic are two-class by nature.
multiclass_how: The c-1 minority classes are each filled up to the majority count (Sec. 3.1, p.1697); a shared class-conditional unit feeds one instance-generation unit per minority class, which outputs convex weights over that class's instances (Sec. 3.2, Eq. 1); labels of generated points are drawn in proportion to (Pc - Pi) (Alg. 1). One c-class classifier, no decomposition.
smote_explanation: GAMO creates each sample as a convex combination of all training points of a minority class (Eq. 1, Sec. 3.2, p.1697), not as a point on a seed-neighbour segment, so there is no single seed and no k-NN partner: a generator network learns the weights adversarially to place points near class peripheries that the classifier gets wrong. Generation runs inside end-to-end training that alternates generator, classifier and discriminator updates (Alg. 1, p.1698), usually in a learned feature space.
corrections: Tested on: Multiclass -> Binary+Multiclass, on the strength of the supplement (Tables 7-8). Decision points: add Seed selection, Sample allocation, Neighbour choice and Inside a pipeline to Placement rule.
flags: BM rests only on the supplement; the main paper alone gives M. Core is debatable: the generator is a learned network and joins the family only through the convex-combination rule.

class_evidence: Framed for binary classification (title; Sec. I, p.31). Eight two-class datasets (Table I, p.33): Abalone9-18, Flare, Wine Quality (KEEL); Haberman (UCI); Customer Churn Wireless Telecom (CrowdAnalytix); Telco Customer Churn, Employee Attrition, Sales Win/Loss (IBM). J48, 5-fold CV (Sec. IV, pp.33-34).
reduced_multiclass: No reduction described; Abalone9-18, Flare and Wine Quality are KEEL two-class versions of multiclass sources.
smote_explanation: As in Borderline-SMOTE, only danger minority points (at least half but not all of their M nearest neighbours are majority) are seeds (Sec. II.B, p.32; Sec. III, pp.32-33). The difference is that the k nearest neighbours, and so the partner, are searched only within the borderline set (Sec. III, Figs. 5-6, p.33). Placement is P'i + gap (P'j - P'i) with gap in [0,1], as in SMOTE (Sec. III, p.33).
corrections: None. Fix the broken character in smote_link (Borderline-SMOTE's).
